tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. Send one or more questions, each with a stable id that will be echoed in the answer.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: describe_image
tools.description: Inspect one image — a local absolute path, an http(s) URL, a complete `[image attachment ...]` note, or a self-contained Markdown attachment reference — and return the text the user needs. Use when the user references an image file or URL, or when a task needs OCR, chart or diagram reading, screenshot or UI analysis, translation of image text, or photo understanding. Always pass an explicit `prompt` with a precise instruction — e.g. "transcribe all text", "extract the table as CSV", "diagnose the UI layout problems", "translate the text into Chinese" — instead of leaving it to the default description: a targeted instruction produces a much more useful answer. If your model accepts image input directly, never call this tool for an image that is already visible to you in the conversation — analyze it with your own vision — and prefer a native image-reading tool (when one is available to you) for local image files. Reserve this tool for images you cannot see: http(s) URLs, `[image attachment …]` notes, or when your model lacks image input entirely. The image may be a local path, an http(s) URL, a complete `[image attachment ...]` note, or — the common case when the user used this plugin's input-box image button — the complete Markdown image reference like `![图片](/describe-image/raw/sha256:abc?ref=...)` pasted into the conversation. Pass that complete Markdown reference as the `image` value: it carries the durable attachment metadata needed after a host restart or inside a PTC nested tool call. A bare attachment id stays supported only while this host process has seen the upload. The image itself never enters the conversation — only the returned text is shown to you.

image.description: Absolute local image path, http(s) URL, complete [image attachment ...] note, or complete Markdown reference ![图片](/describe-image/raw/<id>?ref=...) from the input box. The complete Markdown reference is durable across host restarts and PTC nested tool calls; a bare attachment id is only a current-process fallback.

prompt.description: Your precise instruction for the vision model about this image (e.g. "transcribe all text", "extract the table as CSV", "diagnose the UI problems", "translate the text"). Prefer a targeted prompt over the generic default description.

dir.description: 插件目录（含 package.json 与 tgz 产物）

dir.description: 目标目录（绝对路径，不存在则创建）

description.description: 一句话描述

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

agent_id.description: The agent id of the running agent to interrupt.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

tools.name: ssh_cluster
tools.description: Run one command concurrently across many SSH hosts (all hosts, or filtered by aliases / environment / tags). Triggers: run on all servers, batch operation, production servers, cluster command.

aliases.description: Explicit alias list; when absent every configured host matches.

environment.description: Only hosts with this environment label.

tags.description: Only hosts carrying ALL these tags.

tools.name: ssh_download
tools.description: Download a remote FILE from a configured SSH host to a local path on this machine. Directory download is not supported — download files individually. Triggers: download file from server, fetch remote log/artifact.

localPath.description: Absolute destination path on this machine.

tools.name: ssh_exec
tools.description: Execute a command on a configured SSH host by alias. Prefer combining independent read-only queries into one command. Triggers: run command on server, deploy, check server/status, service control, view logs, any remote operation.

command.description: The shell command to run remotely.

tools.name: ssh_list
tools.description: List configured SSH hosts (alias, host, user, auth, environment, tags, description). Use ssh_exec etc. with the alias. Triggers: SSH, remote server, server IP/hostname, connect/login, check server/status, deploy, upload/download, jump host, tunnel, port forward.

query.description: Optional fuzzy match against alias, description, host, and tags.

tools.name: ssh_tunnel
tools.description: Manage local port-forward tunnels to a configured SSH host. Start a tunnel to reach a remote internal service (database, web UI, API) through 127.0.0.1 on this machine. Triggers: tunnel, port forward, connect database, access internal service.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

The Skill tool normally activates them automatically; call this once only after a direct Skill invocation when the visual tools are still absent. This activation tool disappears after success.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

matches.line: * `dsh plugin --profile <name> <args...>` — profile plugin management as a
* `dsh --profile tui --resume abc` boots the tui profile with `--resume abc`,
* and `dsh --profile web -h` prints the web app's help, not this one's.
* `web` is a hardcoded alias for `--profile web`; `plugin` manages a profile's
dsh --profile web                          boot the web profile (same as: dsh web)
dsh --profile headless "run the tests"     answer one task, print the result, and exit
dsh --profile tui --patch ./extra.yml      boot a custom profile with one extra overlay
dsh --profile tui --resume <session>       arguments after the launcher flags reach the app

For a NEW profile, I probably only need package.json (bundles + deps) + cordis.patch.yml; the loader composes cordis.yml from bundles on first boot (initialized on first use — the `dsh plugin --profile` help says "initialized on first use"). The web profile's cordis.yml was probably generated. I'll create the mathmodel profile with just package.json + patch and let DSH compose the rest on boot.    - P3-2: launch on port 3100, boot verify.
   - P3-3: PRODUCT_UI_GATE (live checks on 3100): G1 shell renders 3-column; G2 dashboard cards; G3 workbench (registry/quiz/mastery APIs); G4 agent H1-style; G5 tutor H4-style; G6 session restore; G7 web profile (3080) remains stock DSH (no shell, no mathmodel tombstones violated — actually web profile currently has shell-v2 + mathmodeling installed from earlier session!    - P3-4: scripts: `scripts/mathmodel-profile-install.ps1` (create/update profile, idempotent), `scripts/mathmodel-profile-start.ps1` (launch on 3100), maybe stop script.

{"content":"# MathModel Workbench — Product PRD

**Date:** 2026-08-25
**Status:** Authoritative product requirements (consolidates `PRODUCT.md`, P1 plugin slice, Shell V2 gate evidence, Phase 3 direction)
**Companion docs:** `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `MATHMODEL_PROFILE_PHASE3_PLAN.md`, `research/DSH_PROFILE_DISTRIBUTION_RESEARCH.md`

---

## 1. Positioning

AI 学习与竞赛工作台：教「为什么」与建模结构，而不是替代思考。
Target user: 参加 0–2 次数模赛的本科生 — 知道部分算法名，但拆题 / 数据 / 特征 / 验证薄弱。

## 2. Core loop

学习 → 训练 → 实战 → 评审 → 找差距 → 专项训练 → 再实战

## 3. Product surface (Shell V2 — verified by SHELL_V2_GATE PASS)

Three-column shell in a **dedicated DSH profile**:

```text
┌────────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│ nav        │ workbench (center)       │ native Agent chat │
│ 仪表盘     │ Dashboard / 工作台 /     │ /modeling-tutor   │
│ 建模工作台 │ 训练 / 竞赛 / 习题 /     │ session-scoped    │
│ 训练…画像  │ 案例 / 论文 / 画像       │ ModelingContext   │
│ + official │                          │                   │
│   sidebar  │                          │                   │
└────────────┴──────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘
```

- Agent 对话为第一等公民（右栏原生会话），`/modeling-tutor` 读取 ModelingContext + Registry。
- 工作台能力（P1 已交付，保持不破坏）：Model Atlas（13 模型注册表）、K-Means 交互课程、Quiz、Mastery、modeling-tutor skill。
- 占位模块（训练/竞赛/习题/案例/论文/画像）显示规划卡片，不空屏。

## 4. Distribution (decided)

| Surface | Content |
|---|---|
| `web` profile | **原版 DSH** — 用户自己的插件生态，产品不注入、不修改 |
| `mathmodel` profile | 产品专用：`dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app` + `@math-modeling/dsh-mathmodeling` + `@math-modeling/shell-v2`；patch 关闭 `ui-layout`（Shell V2 拥有 root） |
| 端口 | 产品实例 3100（web 3080 不变） |

Install/run/remove 见 `scripts/mathmodel-profile-*.ps1`；机制依据 `research/DSH_PROFILE_DISTRIBUTION_RESEARCH.md`。

## 5. Acceptance — PRODUCT_UI_GATE (blocking for GitHub Integration phases)

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| G1 | `mathmodel` profile 实例启动，Shell V2 三栏渲染，8 导航项，零 console error |
| G2 | Dashboard 注册表卡片可见并可点击进入工作台（context POST 发生） |
| G3 | 工作台 API 健康：registry / quizzes / quiz-submit(mastery) / context |
| G4 | 原生 Agent 会话可收发（H1 等效） |
| G5 | `/modeling-tutor` 返回模型上下文相关教学回答（H4 等效） |
| G6 | 刷新恢复会话与 Shell（H2 等效） |
| G7 | `web` profile (3080) 为原版 DSH：无 Shell V2、无数模注入残留，sidebar/composer 正常 |

## 6. Non-goals (until gate passes)

MathMN-lite · czy-provider · 题库 · 案例库 · 论文评审 V2 — 见 Phase 3 plan §Deferred。

## 7. MVP success (unchanged from PRODUCT.md)

现场可稳定跑通 DEMO.md A–D；无 Critical；刷新不丢 demo 用户数据。

block.text:
CLI arg order issue: `--profile mathmodel` must come AFTER `web`? No wait — the error says "web takes none of parent --profile". Looking at bin.js: `dsh web` is an alias command for --profile web, and the `web` command rejects parent --profile flag. So correct syntax: `dsh --profile mathmodel --port 3100 --no-open`? Hmm — from help: `dsh --profile web` boots the web profile. And "web is a hardcoded alias for --profile web". So for a NON-web profile name, use `dsh --profile mathmodel` — but then how do web app flags get passed? "arguments after the launcher flags reach the app": `dsh --profile tui --resume abc` → args reach the app. So: `dsh --profile mathmodel --port 3100 --no-open`? But --port is a web-app flag parsed by the web app's own commander... The launcher passes through unknown args to the profile's app. The web command form (`dsh web --port`) publishes flags; the `--profile X` form passes `[args...]` through to the app.

So correct: `node bin.js --profile mathmodel --port 3100 --no-open`. The app booted for profile mathmodel — how does it know to run the WEB app vs another app? The profile's bundles include dsh-web-app → the profile's "app" is web. The positional args (--port 3100 --no-open) reach the web app.

Fix the start script accordingly.

entries.description: 飞书云空间（云盘/云存储）：管理 Drive 文件和文件夹，包含上传/下载、创建文件夹、复制/移动/删除、查看元数据、评论/权限/订阅、标题、版本和本地文件导入。用户需要整理云盘目录、处理云空间资源 URL/token，或导入 Word/Markdown/Excel/CSV/PPTX/.base 为 docx/sheet/bitable/slides 时使用；doubao.com 云空间 URL/token 也按资源路径和 token 路由，不回退 WebFetch。不负责：文档内容编辑（走 lark-doc）、表格/Base 表内数据操作（走 lark-sheets/lark-base）、知识空间节点/成员管理（走 lark-wiki）、原生 Markdown 文件读写/patch/diff（走 lark-markdown）。

entries.name: lark-event
entries.description: Lark/Feishu real-time event listening / subscribing / consuming: stream events as NDJSON via `lark-cli event consume <EventKey>` (covers IM messages/reactions/chat changes, VC meeting ended, Minutes generated, Whiteboard updated, etc.). Use for Lark bots, real-time message processing, long-running subscribers, streaming webhook/push handlers. Supports `--max-events` / `--timeout` bounded runs and a stderr ready-marker contract — designed for AI agents running as subprocesses.

entries.name: lark-im
entries.description: 飞书即时通讯：收发消息和管理群聊。发送和回复消息、搜索聊天记录、管理群聊成员、上传下载图片和文件（支持大文件分片下载）、管理表情回复、发送应用内/短信/电话加急。当用户需要发消息、查看或搜索聊天记录、下载聊天中的文件、查看群成员、搜索群、创建群聊或话题群、管理标记数据、管理 Feed 置顶（添加/移除/查询置顶会话）、管理标签数据时使用。

entries.name: lark-mail
entries.description: 飞书邮箱 — draft, compose, send, reply, forward, read, and search emails; manage drafts, folders, labels, contacts, attachments, and mail rules. Use when user mentions 起草邮件, 写一封邮件, 拟邮件, 草稿, 发通知邮件, 发送邮件, 发邮件, 回复邮件, 转发邮件, 查看邮件, 看邮件, 读邮件, 搜索邮件, 查邮件, 收件箱, 邮件会话, 编辑草稿, 管理草稿, 下载附件, 邮件文件夹, 邮件标签, 邮件联系人, 监听新邮件, 收信规则, 邮件规则, draft, compose, send email, reply, forward, inbox, mail thread, mail rules.

entries.name: lark-markdown
entries.description: 飞书 Markdown：查看、创建、上传、编辑和比较 Markdown 文件。当用户需要创建或编辑 Markdown 文件、读取、修改、局部 patch 或比较差异时使用。不负责将 Markdown 导入为飞书在线文档，也不负责文件搜索、权限、评论、移动、删除等云空间管理操作。

entries.name: lark-minutes
entries.description: 飞书妙记：搜索妙记列表、查看妙记基础信息、下载妙记音视频文件、上传音视频生成妙记、更新妙记标题、替换说话人。当需要获取、操作或者生成妙记时使用。也支持将本地音视频文件转成纪要和逐字稿（优先使用本 skill，不要用 ffmpeg/whisper 本地转写）。不负责：获取会议关联妙记，或仅按自然语言标题定位纪要

entries.name: lark-note
entries.description: 飞书会议纪要（Note）直查：已知 note_id 时查询纪要详情、展示类型、关联文档 token，并读取 unified 原始逐字记录。当用户已持有 note_id，或从文档显式 vc-node-id 获得 note_id 时使用。不负责会议/日程/妙记定位、文档标题搜索或 Docx 正文读取。

entries.name: lark-okr
entries.description: 飞书 OKR：管理目标与关键结果。查看和编辑 OKR 周期、目标、关键结果、对齐关系、量化指标和进展记录。当用户需要查看或创建 OKR、管理目标和关键结果、查看对齐关系时使用。不负责：待办任务管理（lark-task）、日程/会议安排（lark-calendar）、绩效评估

entries.name: lark-openapi-explorer

entries.name: lark-shared

entries.name: lark-sheets

entries.name: lark-skill-maker

entries.name: lark-slides
entries.description: 飞书幻灯片：创建和编辑幻灯片。创建演示文稿、读取幻灯片内容、管理幻灯片页面（创建、删除、读取、局部替换）。当用户需要创建或编辑幻灯片、读取或修改单个页面时使用。当用户给出 doubao.com 的 /slides/ URL/token 时，也应直接使用本 skill，不要因为域名不是飞书而回退到 WebFetch；路由依据是 URL 路径模式和 token，而不是域名。不负责：云文档内容编辑（走 lark-doc）、云文档里的独立画板对象（走 lark-whiteboard，注意 slide 内嵌的流程图/架构图仍属本 skill）、上传或下载普通文件（走 lark-drive）。

entries.name: lark-task
entries.description: 飞书任务：管理任务、清单和任务智能体。创建待办任务、查看和更新任务状态、拆分子任务、组织任务清单、分配协作成员、上传任务附件、注册或注销任务智能体、更新任务智能体的主页数据、写入智能体任务记录。当用户需要创建待办事项、查看任务列表、跟踪任务进度、管理项目清单或给他人分配任务、为任务上传附件文件、注册注销任务智能体、更新智能体主页数据、写入任务记录时使用。

entries.name: lark-vc

tools.name: describe_image
tools.description: Inspect one image — a local absolute path, an http(s) URL, a complete `[image attachment ...]` note, or a self-contained Markdown attachment reference — and return the text the user needs. Use when the user references an image file or URL, or when a task needs OCR, chart or diagram reading, screenshot or UI analysis, translation of image text, or photo understanding. Always pass an explicit `prompt` with a precise instruction — e.g. "transcribe all text", "extract the table as CSV", "diagnose the UI layout problems", "translate the text into Chinese" — instead of leaving it to the default description: a targeted instruction produces a much more useful answer. If your model accepts image input directly, never call this tool for an image that is already visible to you in the conversation — analyze it with your own vision — and prefer a native image-reading tool (when one is available to you) for local image files. Reserve this tool for images you cannot see: http(s) URLs, `[image attachment …]` notes, or when your model lacks image input entirely. The image may be a local path, an http(s) URL, a complete `[image attachment ...]` note, or — the common case when the user used this plugin's input-box image button — the complete Markdown image reference like `![图片](/describe-image/raw/sha256:abc?ref=...)` pasted into the conversation. Pass that complete Markdown reference as the `image` value: it carries the durable attachment metadata needed after a host restart or inside a PTC nested tool call. A bare attachment id stays supported only while this host process has seen the upload. The image itself never enters the conversation — only the returned text is shown to you.

The complete Markdown reference is durable across host restarts and PTC nested tool calls; a bare attachment id is only a current-process fallback.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background agent's current turn by its agent id. The target may be your direct child or a deeper agent created under you. Only the current turn stops: messages already queued for the agent stay parked until a later send_message, agents it started keep running, and the agent itself stays available for follow-ups. This call returns as soon as the stop request is accepted, so the target may keep running briefly; interrupting an agent that already finished is an accepted no-op.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List your continuable background subagents by durable id and label. Use it to recall which ones you started, not to poll for completion — you are told when one finishes. Status comes from the live registry: running means the agent is working right now, idle means it is loaded but between turns (it may be waiting on agents it started), and ready means it exists only in storage — resumable, not terminal, and not a result waiting to be collected; a `send_message` starts a new turn on the same conversation, and a direct child remains a `send_message` candidate in every status. The snapshot is not a delivery promise — `send_message` performs the authoritative check and may still fail. Children that could not be read are reported as diagnostics instead of being silently dropped. Scope `descendants` walks the whole tree below you in stable pre-order, annotating each entry with its durable direct-parent session id and depth. You may use `send_message` only for depth-1 entries; deeper entries are candidates for `interrupt_agent` only.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children only; descendants walks the complete tree below you.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

The Skill tool normally activates them automatically; call this once only after a direct Skill invocation when the visual tools are still absent. This activation tool disappears after success.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

1: # MathModel Harness — Product PRD & MVP
2: 
3: **Version:** 0.3 draft  
4: **Date:** 2026-08-25  
5: **Product:** MathModel Harness — AI 数学建模学习与竞赛工作台  
6: **Platform:** Dedicated DeepSeek Harness `mathmodel` Profile
7: 
8: ## 1. Product statement
9: 
10: MathModel Harness is an AI-native mathematical-modeling learning and competition environment for students who know scattered algorithms but do not yet have a reliable modeling process.
11: 
12: It does not optimize for:
13: 
14: > 一键把比赛答案生成出来。
15: 
16: It optimizes for:
17: 
18: > 学会为什么这样建模，并在真实比赛中把学习、实验、验证、写作和复盘连成一个闭环。
19: 
20: Core loop:
21: 
22: ```text
23: Learn
24: → Practice
25: → Solve
26: → Review
27: → Diagnose
28: → Retrain
29: → Learn
30: ```
31: 
32: ## 2. Primary user
33: 
34: Primary persona:
35: 
36: > 参加过 0–2 次数学建模比赛的本科生。
37: 
38: Typical state:
39: 
40: - knows names such as AHP, TOPSIS, K-Means, ARIMA, PSO
41: - lacks a stable problem-decomposition framework
42: - weak at data diagnosis and feature engineering
43: - chooses models by familiarity instead of assumptions
44: - often lacks baseline, validation and robustness checks
45: - can write code but cannot explain method fit
46: - paper writing is disconnected from experiments
47: - does not know what weakness to train next
48: 
49: ## 3. Core jobs
50: 
51: ### Learn
52: 
53: “I know the model name but not why it works or when it fails.”
54: 
55: ### Practice
56: 
57: “Give me real data/problems and let me practice decomposition, preprocessing, features, model selection and validation.”
58: 
59: ### Compete
60: 
61: “Help organize competition work without fabricating experiments.”
62: 
63: ### Review
64: 
65: “Tell me exactly where my scheme is weak.”
66: 
67: ### Improve
68: 
69: “Turn competition/reviewer weaknesses into targeted future training.”
70: 
71: ## 4. Product differentiation
72: 
73: Most existing math-modeling AI products are strongest at:
74: 
75: ```text
76: Problem
77: → Model
78: → Code
79: → Paper
80: ```
81: 
82: MathModel adds:
83: 
84: ```text
85: Knowledge
86: → Guided Practice
87: → Competition
88: → Evidence Review
89: → Ability Diagnosis
90: → Personalized Retraining
91: ```
92: 
93: The differentiator is the learning ↔ competition feedback loop.
94: 
95: ## 5. Product principles
96: 
97: 1. Teach why before automating how.
98: 2. Evidence before claims.
99: 3. Baseline before complicated models.
100: 4. Data assumptions before algorithm recommendation.
101: 5. Feature engineering is first-class.
102: 6. Validation is mandatory.
103: 7. AI autonomy is explicit.
104: 8. Competition mistakes become learning tasks.
105: 9. Excellent papers are distilled, not copied.
106: 10. Reuse DSH Agent/Session/Tools instead of recreating them.
107: 
108: ## 6. Agent modes
109: 
110: ### Coach Mode
111: 
112: - Socratic questioning
113: - hints before complete answers
114: - trains variables/assumptions/reasoning
115: 
116: ### Copilot Mode
117: 
118: - collaborative suggestions
119: - partial code
120: - alternatives
121: - user confirms key decisions
122: 
123: ### Agent Mode
124: 
125: - executes confirmed workflow
126: - records parameters/seeds/results
127: - no fabricated experimental output
128: - human confirmation at important gates

275: User: “为什么要标准化？”

278: 
279: ## 12. Daily Review
280: 
281: Train modeling ability, not only definitions.
282: 
283: Question types:
284: 
285: - remember
286: - understand
287: - apply
288: - modeling judgment
289: - modeling error diagnosis
290: - leakage diagnosis
291: - validation choice
292: - feature reasoning
293: 
294: Sources:
295: 
296: ```text
297: weak knowledge units
298: competition mistakes
299: reviewer findings
300: due concepts
301: ```
302: 
303: MVP:
304: 
305: ```text
306: quiz attempt
307: → mastery
308: → due queue
309: ```
310: 
311: ## 13. Modeling Gym
312: 
313: MVP flow:
314: 
315: ```text
316: problem
317: → student proposes variables/objective/constraints/preprocessing/features/models
318: → Coach hint
319: → submit
320: → dimension feedback
321: → recommended training
322: ```
323: 
324: One excellent case is better than many shallow cases.
325: 
326: ## 14. Competition Workbench
327: 
328: Stages:
329: 
330: ```text
331: Read Problem
332: → Decompose
333: → Data Doctor
334: → EDA
335: → Feature Engineering
336: → Model Selection
337: → Algorithm Lab
338: → Validation
339: → Visualization
340: → Paper
341: → Reviewer
342: ```
343: 
344: Each stage produces an artifact.
345: 
346: No raw developer JSON as the primary UI.
347: 
348: ## 15. Data Doctor
349: 
350: Diagnose:
351: 
352: - missingness
353: - data type
354: - temporal/spatial order
355: - leakage
356: - scale
357: - outliers
358: - target availability
359: - informative missingness
360: 
361: Every recommendation explains why/risk/when-not-to-use.
362: 
363: ## 16. Feature Engineering
364: 
365: Every feature gets a Feature Card:
366: 
367: ```text
368: name
369: formula
370: meaning
371: why it may matter
372: risk
373: possible leakage
374: how to validate
375: ```
376: 
377: ## 17. Model Selector
378: 
379: Default output:
380: 
381: ```text
382: Baseline
383: Main
384: Alternative
385: ```
386: 
387: Each recommendation includes fit, assumptions, strengths, risks and validation plan.
388: 
389: ## 18. Algorithm Lab
390: 
391: Experiment record:
392: 
393: ```text
394: algorithm
395: parameters
396: seed
397: runtime
398: metrics
399: objective
400: feasibility
401: artifacts
402: ```
403: 
404: No fabricated run.
405: 
406: ## 19. Problem Library
407: 
408: MVP:
409: 
410: - 5–10 curated benchmark problems
411: - metadata/links where copyright limits redistribution
412: - competition/year/type/tags
413: - common failure modes
414: - validation targets
415: 
416: Not a one-click answer generator.
417: 
418: ## 20. Case Library
419: 
420: Excellent papers are distilled into structured cases.
421: 
422: Schema:
423: 
424: ```text
425: problem structure
426: subproblems
427: data processing
428: feature engineering
429: baseline
430: main model
431: alternatives
432: algorithm
433: validation
434: robustness
435: figures
436: writing structure
437: innovation
438: strengths
439: weaknesses
440: transferable lessons
441: ```
442: 
443: MVP: 3 cases covering evaluation, forecasting, optimization.
444: 
445: ## 21. Reverse Case Training
446: 
447: ```text
448: Problem
449: → hide excellent solution
450: → student proposes plan
451: → compare against distilled case
452: → gap analysis
453: → recommended training
454: ```
455: 
456: ## 22. Paper Reviewer
457: 
458: Training rubric, not official competition score.
459: 
460: Dimensions:
461: 
462: - problem understanding
463: - data handling
464: - feature engineering
465: - model reasonableness
466: - mathematical rigor
467: - algorithm/solution
468: - validation
469: - interpretation
470: - innovation
471: - visualization
472: - writing
473: - reproducibility
474: 
475: Findings feed Profile/Daily Review.
476: 
477: ## 23. Modeling Profile
478: 
479: Track:
480: 
481: - modeling dimensions
482: - model mastery
483: - knowledge-unit mastery
484: - recent mistakes
485: - reviewer weaknesses
486: - competition history
487: 
488: Competition learning bridge:
489: 
490: ```text
491: recommended DBSCAN
492: → mastery 20%
493: → 5-minute quick lesson
494: → return to project
495: ```
496: 
497: ## 24. MVP levels
498: 
499: ### Demo MVP
500: 
501: 1. dedicated `mathmodel` profile boots
502: 2. coherent MathModel shell
503: 3. Dashboard
504: 4. Model Atlas
505: 5. polished K-Means + Canvas
506: 6. contextual `/modeling-tutor`
507: 7. Quiz → mastery
508: 8. one Gym case
509: 9. Competition demo: problem → Data Doctor → Model Selector
510: 10. Paper Reviewer → Gap
511: 11. Profile reflects learning feedback
512: 
513: ### Product MVP
514: 
515: Adds:
516: 
517: 1. profile installer/bootstrap
518: 2. 5–10 Problems
519: 3. 3 distilled Cases
520: 4. baseline/main/alternative experiments
521: 5. first real Algorithm Provider executions
522: 6. persistent project artifacts
523: 7. contract/manifest/claim-ledger lite
524: 8. basic scientific visualization templates
525: 9. stable remove/rollback
526: 10. documented supported DSH version
527: 
528: ## 25. Non-goals
529: 
530: Not required for MVP:
531: 
532: - 30 polished lessons
533: - full deep learning catalog
534: - automatic award-paper generation
535: - teacher/admin multi-user system
536: - full FSRS
537: - unrestricted code execution
538: - full LangGraph orchestration
539: - OpenHands as primary core
540: - full historical archive
541: - redistribution of copyrighted paper PDFs
542: 
543: ## 26. Success criteria
544: 
545: A user can complete:
546: 
547: ```text
548: open MathModel
549: → learn K-Means
550: → ask why
551: → quiz
552: → mastery changes
553: → training case
554: → Coach feedback
555: → competition project
556: → diagnose data
557: → compare models
558: → review paper
559: → weakness enters Profile
560: ```
561: 
562: Architecture success:
563: 
564: - `web` profile untouched
565: - `mathmodel` independently boots
566: - no second LLM chat backend
567: - context isolation passes
568: - one sidebar
569: - Workbench dominates screen
570: - removal has no effect on normal DSH
571: 
572: Quality:
573: 
574: ```text
575: Critical = 0
576: demo-blocking High = 0
577: ```
578: 
579: ## 27. UX target
580: 
581: Desktop:
582: 
583: ```text
584: 220px | flexible Workbench | 380–420px Agent
585: ```
586: 
587: Do not repeat current Shell V2 mistake of embedding the full official DSH sidebar below MathModel navigation.
588: 
589: ## 28. Positioning summary
590: 
591: > MathModel Harness 是一个基于 DeepSeek Harness 的数学建模专用 AI 工作台，把模型学习、专项训练、比赛执行、论文评审和个人能力诊断连成一个闭环。
592: 
593: > 不是“AI 帮你交一篇答案”，而是“AI 帮你逐渐真正学会建模，并在比赛里可靠地使用这些能力”。

# DSH Profile / Bundle Distribution Research

**Date:** 2026-08-25  
**Target repository:** `John030427/math-modeling-workbench`  
**Target branch:** `experiment/mathmodel-harness`

## Executive Decision

Recommended architecture:

# **MathModel Harness = dedicated `mathmodel` DSH Profile + standard MathModel Bundles**

Do not make the user's ordinary `web` profile the primary product target, and do not maintain a full fork of DeepSeek Harness unless a future hard API limitation makes composition impossible.

```text
DeepSeek Harness installation
│
├── profile: web
│     └── normal DSH, untouched
│
└── profile: mathmodel
      ├── @deepseek-ai/dsh-base
      ├── @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app
      ├── @math-modeling/mathmodel-suite
      │     ├── MathModel Shell
      │     ├── Modeling Core
      │     ├── Modeling Skills
      │     ├── Modeling Tools
      │     ├── Learning State
      │     └── Registry
      └── profile-local user overrides
```

Normal DSH and MathModel Harness become two different compositions of the same upstream runtime.

## 1. What upstream DSH explicitly supports

DeepSeek Harness states that every major part of the product is a Cordis plugin, including model adapters, tools, session log, agent loop and UI layers.

Official concepts:

```text
Bundle = what the author distributes
Profile = what the user boots
```

A bundle declares `dsh.bundle` and contributes a `cordis.patch.yml`. A profile declares the ordered `dsh.profile.bundles` list.

The final composition can be inspected with:

```bash
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config
```

Official references:

- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/architecture.md
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/bundle/README.md

I can't easily find the reflect read API from minified-ish code. Rather than burn more time reverse-engineering, choose a more robust and simpler mechanism for U4 (suppress duplicate 数模工作台 tab in harness mode):

**Option A: URL/profile-driven flag via host part.** mathmodel-suite's HOST side sets something the client can read... client reads window.__DSH_BOOT__ which contains entries — the shell could check if a specific marker exists. Actually simpler: **the shell itself owns root; it can strip/ignore conversation.view tabs? No — tabs render inside native conversation component.**

**Option B: profile patch disables the specific loader entry that registers the tab?** The tab registration lives inside dsh-mathmodeling's client apply — can't disable partially via patch.

**Option C: dsh-mathmodeling checks a global set by shell at module-load time.** Both clients load via ModuleLoader with `immediately: true`. Load order = boot entries order. In __DSH_BOOT__ entries array, order follows assembly order (bundles order → suite before/after?). Fragile but controllable: suite patch inserts shell BEFORE mathmodeling entry, and shell's client.js first line sets `window.__MM_SHELL_HOST__ = true` synchronously at module load (not in apply — at ModuleLoader factory execution). Then dsh-mathmodeling's apply checks `window.__MM_SHELL_HOST__` at registration time (apply runs after both modules loaded anyway since apply happens during fiber start after module eval). Actually module evaluation order matters only for the window flag set; apply-time check is safe as long as shell module evaluated before mathmodeling APPLY runs. Apply runs per-plugin after all modules load? Client modules each load+apply sequentially per entry order. If mathmodeling applies BEFORE shell module evaluates, flag not yet set. To be safe: mathmodeling defers its decision to a microtask/next tick? Ugly.

**Option D (cleanest): config via profile patch on the mathmodeling entry.** cordis.patch.yml supports id-targeted CONFIG overrides. The client receives config? Does dsh.client support config passing to client apply? Unknown.

**Option E: separate compatibility surface by package build.** The plan says "Compatibility plugin mode may keep it" — the DUPLICATE TAB is registered by dsh-mathmodeling unconditionally. What if the SUITE provides its own domain integration instead of reusing dsh-mathmodeling's client registrations... no, too big.

**Option F: shell removes the tab after registration.** ctx.slots has inject/register; is there an unregister-by-id API accessible? The shell could call ctx.slots.unregister? Unknown API.

Reconsider Option C with guaranteed ordering: __DSH_BOOT__ entries array — I saw earlier the web profile boot list had explicit ordering with inject/immediately flags. The composed order comes from bundle/patch insert order. Suite patch can control insert order deterministically:
```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mathmodel-shell
      name: '@math-modeling/mathmodel-shell'
    - id: dsh-mathmodeling
      name: '@math-modeling/dsh-mathmodeling'
```
Insert order within one patch block should preserve array order into the loader → boot entries follow same order → shell module evaluates first → sets window flag → mathmodeling apply sees flag. The spike relied on similar ordering assumptions ("Package sets dsh.client.immediately=true so this runs before late footer plugins") — precedent exists.

Even safer belt-and-braces: dsh-mathmodeling checks the flag BOTH at apply AND inside a `setTimeout(0)` re-check? No — keep simple: flag check at apply + shell module top-level assignment. Verify empirically in live test (the whole point of the loop). If ordering fails (tab still appears), fallback: also gate on hostname/port? No. Another robust signal: shell sets `document.documentElement.dataset.mmShellHost='1'` at module eval; mathmodeling checks at apply AND retries once on next microtask... Keep it simple first, verify visually.

Hmm wait — actually there's an even MORE deterministic approach: **mathmodeling decides based on ui-layout absence!** In harness mode, ui-layout is disabled → never provides 'layout' service... but mathmodel-shell PROVIDES layout stub (needed by ui-sidebar... which we're REMOVING per U1!). With single-sidebar design, we drop the sidebar seat entirely → ui-sidebar has nothing to attach → does ui-sidebar crash without layout?? ui-sidebar injects ctx.layout (stub provided by shell). If ui-sidebar isn't rendered anywhere, its apply still runs (it's in dsh-base bundle) — it registers slots for a 'sidebar' seat nobody renders. Harmless as long as boot doesn't abort. Spike lesson said replacing root must RE-DECLARE official children sidebar/conversation/details/shell.overlay "or the client boot fails" — because plugins register INTO those seats at boot; if seat missing → abort. So my root declaration MUST still declare all official children even if I don't render some? Currently I render sidebar seat; if I stop rendering it but keep declaring it in children map, do registrations still work (slot exists but owner doesn't render)? Slot registry vs rendering are separate — declaring children defines the slot contract; ShellFrame chooses what to render. thinking-counter race happened because footer seat was declared by ui-sidebar only AFTER layout existed (timing), not because of rendering. Keeping the declaration + dropping the render should be OK — BUT ui-sidebar's own component then never renders → sessions list gone (accepted per U1).

So detection heuristic: mathmodeling asks ctx.reflect whether 'root' slot owner is NOT ui-layout? There's a slots catalog API? Too deep.

DECISION: Go with window/document flag set at shell module evaluation + ordered inserts in suite patch. Empirically verified via screenshots (U4 check). Simple, reversible, documented in dsh-compat notes.
